title: Jason Arday found dead
byline: Charles Hymas, Albert Tait, Gordon Rayner
excerpt: Academic had resigned from the University of Cambridge last week
content_html:
Academic had resigned from the University of Cambridge last week

Jason Arday, the former University of Cambridge professor, has been found dead.

Mr Arday was found “unresponsive” at an address in Battersea, south London, on Friday afternoon. He was later pronounced dead at the scene.

A spokesman for the Metropolitan Police said officers were called by the London Ambulance Service at 3.12pm on Friday.

He said: “Sadly, a 41-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene. His next-of-kin have been informed and are being supported by officers.

“At this time his death is being treated as unexpected, but is not believed to be suspicious. The case is being investigated by officers from the Met’s Central South Command Unit. A file will be prepared for the coroner.”

The London Ambulance Service said it had been called to the scene at 3.06pm.

A spokesman said the service had dispatched an ambulance crew, an advanced paramedic in a fast response car and members of its Hazardous Area Response Team.

“Sadly, a person was pronounced dead at the scene,” the spokesman said.

Police erected a cordon around the address where Mr Arday’s body was found.

A black private ambulance was seen arriving at around 8pm. It was seen leaving the address just before 8.30pm.

Mr Arday is survived by his wife and two children. His family paid tribute to him as a “gentle man” and an “amazing father, partner, brother, uncle and son”.

“Jason was subjected to a campaign of sustained abuse for the more than three years since he accepted the role of professor at Cambridge University by those who would leave no stone unturned in their quest to undermine him,” they said in a statement.

“The campaign of misinformation was too much for Jason, who was a gentle man and who always wanted to see the best in everyone. We are in shock to have lost this amazing father, partner, brother, uncle and son.”

Born in 1985, Mr Arday went to a state primary school in Battersea before attending secondary school in nearby Southfields.

He then did a Btec at Merton college in Morden, south London before going on to university.

Mr Arday studied education at undergraduate and postgraduate level, completing his PhD at Liverpool John Moores University, and went on to hold academic posts at the University of Roehampton, Durham University and the University of Glasgow, where he became professor of sociology of education in 2021.

His memoir, titled Great and Unfortunate Things, was published in the United States earlier this week and is due to be published by Simon and Schuster in the UK on Aug 27.

Mr Arday resigned as professor of sociology of education at the University of Cambridge on Aug 5, following accusations of plagiarism. He was the university’s youngest ever black professor.

Last week, Cambridge launched an investigation into Mr Arday’s appointment and tenure at the university. It will feed into a review of the university’s hiring process for all senior academic positions. Mr Arday resigned just a few hours after the university announced the investigation, citing the “unrelenting level of public scrutiny”.

Prof Deborah Prentice, Cambridge’s vice-chancellor, said: “We are desperately saddened to hear this tragic news. Our heartfelt sympathies go to Jason Arday’s family and friends at this incredibly difficult time.”

A spokesman for Durham University said: “We are shocked and terribly sad to learn of the death of Jason Arday. Jason was a member of Durham University’s sociology department between 2019 and 2022.

“He is remembered at Durham as a kind and warm person, who actively sought to promote opportunities for PhD students. We want to express our deepest sympathy to his family who are in our thoughts today.”

Lucy Powell, the Education Secretary, said: “I’m deeply shocked and saddened to hear about the death of Jason Arday.

“My heartfelt condolences are with his friends and family at this very sad time. I urge people to give them privacy through this incredibly difficult period and to remember there are real people with loved ones involved.”

content_html_zh:
上周已从剑桥大学辞职

剑桥大学前教授杰森·阿尔戴被发现死亡。

周五下午，阿戴先生被发现在伦敦南部巴特西的一处地方“没有反应”。 他后来被宣布当场死亡。

大都会警察局发言人表示，周五下午 3 点 12 分，伦敦救护车服务中心向警方报警。

他说：“遗憾的是，一名 41 岁的男子被宣布当场死亡。 他的近亲已收到通知并得到官员的支持。

“目前他的死亡被视为意外，但据信并不可疑。 伦敦警察厅中南指挥部的官员正在调查此案。 将为验尸官准备一份文件。”

伦敦救护车服务中心表示已于下午 3 点 06 分赶到现场。

一名发言人表示，该部门已派出一名救护人员、一名乘坐快速反应车的高级护理人员以及危险区域反应小组的成员。

发言人说：“遗憾的是，现场有人被宣布死亡。”

警方在阿尔代尸体被发现的地址周围拉起了警戒线。

晚上8点左右，一辆黑色私人救护车抵达。 有人看到它在晚上 8.30 之前离开了这个地址。

阿戴先生身后留下了他的妻子和两个孩子。 他的家人称赞他是一个“绅士”和“了不起的父亲、伙伴、兄弟、叔叔和儿子”。

他们在一份声明中表示：“自从杰森接受剑桥大学教授职位以来，三年多来一直受到那些不遗余力地破坏他的人的持续虐待。”

“错误信息的传播对杰森来说实在是太难以忍受了，他是一个温柔的人，总是希望看到每个人最好的一面。 我们对失去这位了不起的父亲、合作伙伴、兄弟、叔叔和儿子感到震惊。”

Arday 先生出生于 1985 年，曾就读于巴特西的一所公立小学，然后在附近的南菲尔德 (Southfields) 上中学。

随后，他在伦敦南部莫登的默顿学院 (Merton College) 攻读了 Btec 学位，然后继续上大学。

Arday 先生学习本科和研究生教育，在利物浦约翰摩尔斯大学完成博士学位，随后在罗汉普顿大学、杜伦大学和格拉斯哥大学担任学术职务，并于 2021 年成为该大学的教育社会学教授。

他的回忆录《伟大而不幸的事情》本周早些时候在美国出版，西蒙和舒斯特出版社将于 8 月 27 日在英国出版。

8 月 5 日，阿戴先生因抄袭指控辞去剑桥大学教育社会学教授职务。 他是该大学有史以来最年轻的黑人教授。

上周，剑桥大学对阿代先生在该大学的任命和任期展开了调查。 它将纳入对大学所有高级学术职位招聘流程的审查。 在该大学宣布调查后几小时，阿尔代先生就辞职了，理由是“公众监督的严格程度”。

剑桥大学副校长黛博拉·普伦蒂斯教授表示：“听到这个悲惨消息，我们感到非常悲伤。 在这个极其困难的时刻，我们向杰森·阿戴的家人和朋友表示衷心的同情。”

杜伦大学发言人表示：“得知杰森·阿尔戴去世的消息，我们感到震惊和悲伤。 Jason 于 2019 年至 2022 年间担任杜伦大学社会学系成员。

“他在达勒姆被认为是一个善良而热情的人，积极寻求为博士生提供机会。 我们想向今天我们思念的他的家人表示最深切的同情。”

教育部长露西·鲍威尔 (Lucy Powell) 表示：“听到杰森·阿戴 (Jason Arday) 去世的消息，我深感震惊和悲伤。

“在这个非常悲伤的时刻，我向他的朋友和家人表示衷心的哀悼。 我敦促人们在这个极其困难的时期给予他们隐私，并记住还有真实的人与亲人参与其中。”
